transport: Two power leads only — red (+), black (-), 12 V or 24 V DC, 14 AWG, ~13 in / 33 cm. No signal terminal, no bus, no connector beyond the 2-pin power lead. Control is a mechanical pressure switch inside the pump head, adjusted with a 2 mm Allen key.
blocks: Nothing to poll and nothing to command. There is no register map to find, so no driver is possible against the pump itself. Any Cabin Hub integration is against a relay upstream of it and a shunt or meter beside it — those are the relay's and the meter's dialects, not SEAFLO's.

downgradedOnReview: The substantive claim survives: every cited source exists and says what is claimed about the absence of a data interface. The 51 Series manual (manuals.plus/ae/1005002661407706) names SFDP1-050-060-51 explicitly and gives leads as "14 AWG, 13\" (33 cm) long with 2-Pin connector" with no RS485/Modbus/CAN. The 52 Series manual covers 52 & 54 Series and the quoted wiring line is verbatim-accurate (2-wire DC, 40 A fuse).
gotchas: SEAFLO publishes no protocol document for any pump, because there is no protocol. Its public Downloads page (seaflo.com, tid=332) offers exactly four items: the 2026 Marine Equipment Catalog, the 2026 Marine Lighting Catalog, the 2026 Ultrasonic Defense System Catalog and the 2025 RV Equipment Catalog. The pressure switch is the only intelligence in the pump and it is not electrically accessible. It is in series inside the head; it does not present its state on a terminal.

Cutting the supply with a relay is safe on this group specifically BECAUSE the pressure switch is internal — the pump self-regulates whenever it has power, so a relay only has to decide 'water system live / dead'. That is not true of the bare-motor group; do not carry the habit across.
SEAFLO's 52 Series manual calls for a 40 A fuse. Do not size the relay or the wiring off the retailer's GPM headline.

The '12V 7.0 GPM 60 PSI continuous duty pump' seen at one retailer matches the 53 Series 12V spec (7 GPM / 60 PSI) exactly. That is a coincidence-shaped match, not evidence — no source names them as the same part. Left as its own line until a model number is seen on a label.
unmappedReports: water-system pressure in PSI / bar — NOT reported by these pumps (the switch acts on it internally and exposes nothing). Recorded because Cabin Hub has no wire name for it either: MetricKind::Pressure is Unit::Hectopascal, a barometric shape. A water-pressure transducer added later has nowhere to land., pump cycle count / duty cycle — not reported by the pump; also has no MetricKind. `pump-run-hours` exists, `flow-rate` exists, but a rapid-cycling pump (the classic failure signature) has no wire name., dry-run / no-prime fault — not reported by the pump; no MetricKind and no fault channel for a pump.
